offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Third Degree Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a public place
While intoxicated (BAC .08 or higher, or loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties by reason of alcohol, drugs, or a combination)
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (Class A Misdemeanor for first offense)
Open container in vehicle (minimum 6 days confinement)
Child passenger under 15 (State Jail Felony under § 49.045)
Third or subsequent offense (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Texas uses 'DWI' (Driving While Intoxicated) rather than 'DUI.' Implied consent under Transportation Code § 724.011. ALR (Administrative License Revocation) hearing available within 15 days.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a public place
While intoxicated
BAC .08 or higher, or loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties
No prior DWI convictions
notes: License suspension 90-365 days. Eligible for deferred adjudication. Surcharges may apply.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second); Third Degree Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a public place while intoxicated
Defendant had one or more prior DWI convictions
notes: Second offense: 180-day to 2-year license suspension. Third+ is a felony. Vehicle forfeiture possible. Ignition interlock may be required.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_min: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a public place
While intoxicated by a controlled substance, drug, dangerous drug, or combination of substances
Resulting in loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must show actual impairment or loss of normal faculties. Blood test typically required.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common DWI plea-down. Relatively light penalties compared to DWI.

statute_title: Accident Involving Personal Injury or Death — Duty to Stop
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor to Second Degree Felony depending on severity
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant knowingly failed to stop and render aid
Defendant failed to provide identification
notes: Failure to stop and render aid resulting in death is a Second Degree Felony (2-20 years). Property-damage-only hit-and-run is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a public place
While intoxicated
By reason of that intoxication caused the death of another by accident or mistake
notes: Texas calls DWI-related deaths 'intoxication manslaughter' rather than vehicular homicide. Second Degree Felony with 2-20 year range.

offense_class: State Jail Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another
By criminal negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Non-intoxication vehicular deaths are typically charged as criminally negligent homicide. Intoxication-related deaths are charged under § 49.08.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class B Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a highway
While the defendant's license was suspended, revoked, or canceled
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
notes: First offense for driving while license invalid without a prior conviction is a fine-only Class C Misdemeanor.

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (prior conviction); State Jail Felony (tire deflation device used against)
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant willfully failed to stop or fled
enhancements: Officer uses tire deflation device (State Jail Felony)
notes: Enhanced to Third Degree Felony if the flight results in bodily injury to another person.

statute_title: Possession of Controlled Substance — Penalty Group 1
offense_class: State Jail Felony (under 1 gram); Third Degree Felony (1-4 grams); Second Degree Felony (4-200 grams); First Degree Felony (200-400 grams); Enhanced First Degree (400+ grams)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Listed in Penalty Group 1 (cocaine, heroin, meth, oxycodone, etc.)
Defendant did not have a valid prescription
mandatory_minimum: 5 years and $10,000 fine (200-400 grams); 10 years and $100,000 fine (400+ grams)
notes: Penalty Group 1 includes cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, oxycodone, and other serious controlled substances. Amount thresholds determine felony level.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (2 oz or less); Class A Misdemeanor (2-4 oz); State Jail Felony (4 oz to 5 lbs); Third Degree Felony (5-50 lbs); Second Degree Felony (50-2000 lbs); enhanced above
penalty_max: 180 days (2 oz or less); 1 year (2-4 oz); 2 years (4 oz-5 lbs); 10 years (5-50 lbs); 20 years (50-2000 lbs); life (2000+ lbs)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a usable quantity of marihuana
notes: Texas has not legalized recreational or medical marijuana (limited CBD oil program exists). Possession of 2 oz or less is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (under 1 gram); Third Degree Felony (1-4 grams); Second Degree Felony (4-200 grams)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third); 20 years (Second); life (200+ grams)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is in Penalty Group 1
Defendant did not have lawful authorization
notes: Any amount of cocaine possession is a felony in Texas. Even residue amounts can be charged as a State Jail Felony.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (under 1 gram); Third Degree Felony (1-4 grams); Second Degree Felony (4-200 grams)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third); 20 years (Second); life (200+ grams)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is in Penalty Group 1
Defendant did not have lawful authorization
notes: Meth is a major enforcement priority in Texas. Any amount is a felony. Manufacturing components may trigger additional charges.

statute_title: Manufacture or Delivery of Controlled Substance — Penalty Group 1
offense_class: State Jail Felony (under 1 gram); Second Degree Felony (1-4 grams); First Degree Felony (4-200 grams); Enhanced First Degree (200+ grams)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance in Penalty Group 1
mandatory_minimum: 10 years and $100,000 fine (200-400 grams); 15 years and $250,000 fine (400+ grams)
notes: Manufacturing or delivery carries significantly higher penalties than possession. Drug-free zone enhancements near schools add penalties.

offense_class: Same as trafficking by amount and penalty group
elements: Defendant delivered a controlled substance to another person
Delivery includes actual transfer, constructive transfer, or offer to sell
notes: Delivery and manufacturing fall under the same statute. Delivery to a minor carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Same as delivery/trafficking by amount and penalty group
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured a controlled substance
Manufacturing includes production, preparation, compounding, or processing
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a child
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine or operating a clandestine lab carries additional charges for endangering public health.

statute_title: Possession or Delivery of Drug Paraphernalia
offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (possession); Class A Misdemeanor (delivery); State Jail Felony (delivery to minor)
penalty_max: Fine only (possession); 1 year (delivery); 2 years (delivery to minor)
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With the intent to use it to introduce a controlled substance into the body
enhancements: Delivery to a minor under 18 (State Jail Felony)
notes: Simple possession of paraphernalia is a fine-only Class C Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a State Jail Felony.

offense_class: Same as delivery by amount and penalty group
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to deliver
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or communications
notes: Intent to deliver is typically inferred from large quantities, packaging materials, scales, baggies, and large amounts of cash.

offense_class: Capital Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another person

Under one of the enumerated aggravating circumstances (murder of peace officer, firefighter, child under 10; murder during commission of kidnapping, burglary, robbery, sexual assault, arson, retaliation; murder for hire; multiple murders in same scheme)
enhancements: Capital murder automatically carries death or life without parole
notes: Texas has the death penalty. Capital murder is the only offense carrying death. If death not sought, mandatory life without parole. Defendant under 18 at time of offense receives mandatory life.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another person
Or intended to cause serious bodily injury and committed an act clearly dangerous to human life that caused the death
Or committed or attempted to commit a felony and in the course of that felony committed an act clearly dangerous that caused the death
notes: Standard murder is a First Degree Felony. If defendant proves sudden passion from adequate cause, punishment is reduced to Second Degree Felony range.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Under the immediate influence of sudden passion arising from adequate cause
Adequate cause means cause that would commonly produce a degree of anger, rage, or terror sufficient to render the mind incapable of cool reflection
notes: Texas does not have a separate voluntary manslaughter statute. Sudden passion is an affirmative defense to murder that reduces punishment to Second Degree Felony range.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
notes: Manslaughter in Texas is a reckless killing. Criminally negligent homicide (§ 19.05) is a lesser included offense.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony; First Degree Felony (against family/household member, public servant, witness, or in retaliation)
elements: Defendant committed assault as defined in § 22.01
And caused serious bodily injury to another
Or used or exhibited a deadly weapon during the assault
enhancements: Against a family member (First Degree Felony)
Against a public servant (First Degree Felony)
notes: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon against a family member is a First Degree Felony with 5-99 year range.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (bodily injury); Class C Misdemeanor (threat or offensive contact)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or intentionally or knowingly threatened another with imminent bodily injury
Or intentionally or knowingly caused physical contact with another when the person knew or should have known the contact would be offensive or provocative
enhancements: Against a public servant, family member, or elderly/disabled person (Third Degree Felony or higher)
notes: Assault against a family member (family violence) can be enhanced. Prior family violence conviction makes subsequent assault a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
notes: Texas combines assault and battery under the single assault statute (§ 22.01). No separate battery offense.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant, in the course of committing theft
Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or intentionally or knowingly threatened or placed another in fear of imminent bodily injury or death
notes: Robbery is theft by violence or threat. Distinguished from aggravated robbery.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery as defined in § 29.02
And caused serious bodily injury to another
Or used or exhibited a deadly weapon
Or the victim was 65+ years old or disabled
notes: Aggravated robbery is a First Degree Felony with 5-99 years or life. One of the most common violent felony charges in Texas.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly abducted another person
notes: Simple kidnapping is a Third Degree Felony. Voluntary release in a safe place is an affirmative defense reducing to a Third Degree Felony even for aggravated kidnapping.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (property); Second Degree Felony (habitation, public building); First Degree Felony (bodily injury or death)
penalty_min: 180 days (State Jail); 2 years (Second Degree); 5 years (First Degree)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 20 years (Second Degree); 99 years or life (First Degree)
elements: Defendant started a fire or caused an explosion
With intent to destroy or damage any building, habitation, or vehicle
Or any property with intent to collect insurance
enhancements: Habitation or place of worship (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Arson of a habitation, place of assembly, or place of worship is a Second Degree Felony. If bodily injury or death results, First Degree Felony.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (attempted murder); First Degree Felony (attempted capital murder)
penalty_max: 20 years (Second Degree); 99 years or life (First Degree)
elements: Defendant intended to commit murder
Defendant did an act amounting to more than mere preparation
That directly tended toward the commission of the offense
The victim survived
notes: Criminal attempt is generally one category lower than the completed offense. Attempted murder (§ 19.02) is a Second Degree Felony.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed an assault as defined in § 22.01
While using or exhibiting a deadly weapon
enhancements: Against a family member (First Degree Felony)
notes: A deadly weapon includes a firearm, knife, or anything manifestly designed, made, or adapted for the purpose of inflicting death or serious bodily injury.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (under $100); Class B Misdemeanor ($100-$750); Class A Misdemeanor ($750-$2,500); State Jail Felony ($2,500-$30,000); Third Degree Felony ($30,000-$150,000); Second Degree Felony ($150,000-$300,000); First Degree Felony ($300,000+)
penalty_max: Fine only to life depending on value
elements: Defendant unlawfully appropriated property
With intent to deprive the owner of property
enhancements: Theft from a person (State Jail Felony minimum)
Theft by public servant (one category higher)
notes: Texas has comprehensive value-based theft thresholds. Theft from a person is always at least a State Jail Felony regardless of amount.

offense_class: State Jail Felony ($2,500-$30,000); Third Degree Felony ($30,000-$150,000); Second Degree Felony ($150,000-$300,000); First Degree Felony ($300,000+)
elements: Defendant unlawfully appropriated property
Value exceeded $2,500
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Felony theft in Texas begins at $2,500. Texas does not use the term 'grand theft' but the felony thresholds serve the same function.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (under $100); Class B Misdemeanor ($100-$750); Class A Misdemeanor ($750-$2,500)
penalty_max: Fine only (Class C); 180 days (Class B); 1 year (Class A)
elements: Defendant unlawfully appropriated property
Value under $2,500
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Misdemeanor theft under $2,500. Two prior convictions enhance a Class C Misdemeanor theft to a Class B.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant unlawfully appropriated merchandise from a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise without paying
enhancements: Organized retail theft (§ 31.16, State Jail Felony)
Using a shielding or deactivation device
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general theft statute. Organized retail theft is a separate State Jail Felony regardless of value.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (vehicle); Second Degree Felony (building); First Degree Felony (habitation)
penalty_min: 180 days (State Jail); 2 years (Second Degree); 5 years (First Degree)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 20 years (Second Degree); 99 years or life (First Degree)
elements: Defendant entered a habitation, building, or vehicle
Without the effective consent of the owner
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault
notes: Burglary of a habitation is a First Degree Felony (5-99 years). Burglary of a building is a Second Degree Felony. Burglary of a vehicle is a State Jail Felony.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant entered a habitation
Without the effective consent of the owner
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault
notes: Habitation includes a structure or vehicle adapted for overnight accommodation. One of the most seriously punished property crimes in Texas.

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of a Motor Vehicle
offense_class: State Jail Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly operated another's boat, airplane, or motor-propelled vehicle
Without the effective consent of the owner
notes: Unauthorized use of a vehicle (UUMV) is always a State Jail Felony regardless of vehicle value. May also be charged as theft based on value.

offense_class: Same classification as theft based on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property
Knowing the property was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Receiving stolen property is prosecuted under the theft statute in Texas.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (under $100); Class B Misdemeanor ($100-$750); Class A Misdemeanor ($750-$2,500); State Jail Felony ($2,500-$30,000); higher for greater amounts
penalty_max: Fine only to 2 years+ depending on value
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly damaged or destroyed property of another
Without the owner's effective consent
notes: Texas uses 'criminal mischief' for property destruction. Value thresholds mirror the theft statute.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (habitation or agricultural land); State Jail Felony (critical infrastructure)
penalty_max: 180 days (Class B); 1 year (Class A); 2 years (State Jail)
elements: Defendant entered or remained on property of another
Without effective consent
And had notice that entry was forbidden (orally, in writing, by fencing, or by signage)
notes: Notice can be oral, written, fencing, or conspicuous signage including purple paint marks.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (under $100) through First Degree Felony ($300,000+)
penalty_max: Fine only to life depending on value
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly damaged or destroyed tangible property of the owner
Without the owner's effective consent
Or intentionally or knowingly tampered with property causing substantial inconvenience
notes: Criminal mischief is Texas's primary property destruction/vandalism offense. Same value thresholds as theft.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Third Degree Felony (prior conviction or strangulation)
elements: Defendant committed an assault as defined in § 22.01
Against a member of the defendant's family, household, or dating partner
enhancements: Prior family violence conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: First offense family violence assault is a Class A Misdemeanor. Second offense or strangulation is a Third Degree Felony. Triggers protective order eligibility and federal firearms prohibition.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Third Degree Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury
To a family member, household member, or dating partner
enhancements: Prior family violence conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Texas combines assault and battery under the assault statute. Family violence context triggers enhanced penalties on repeat offenses.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (endangerment); Second Degree Felony (imminent danger of death, bodily injury, or physical/mental impairment)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence
Placed a child younger than 15 in imminent danger of death, bodily injury, or physical/mental impairment
By act or omission
enhancements: Imminent danger of death or serious injury (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Child endangerment through DWI with a child under 15 is charged separately under § 49.045.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony (reckless/negligent bodily injury); Second Degree Felony (reckless serious injury); First Degree Felony (intentional serious injury)
penalty_min: 2 years (Third Degree); 2 years (Second Degree); 5 years (First Degree)
penalty_max: 10 years (Third Degree); 20 years (Second Degree); 99 years or life (First Degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence
Caused bodily injury to a child (under 15)
Or an elderly individual (65+) or disabled individual
enhancements: Intentional serious bodily injury (First Degree Felony)
notes: Injury to a child, elderly, or disabled person. Intentional or knowing serious bodily injury is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Third Degree Felony (two or more prior violations or prior family violence conviction)
elements: A protective order was in effect
Defendant intentionally or knowingly violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Two or more prior violations (Third Degree Felony)
Prior family violence conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Continuous violation of a protective order (§ 25.072) — two or more violations in 12 months — is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony; Second Degree Felony (prior conviction)
penalty_max: 10 years (Third Degree); 20 years (Second Degree with prior)
elements: Defendant on more than one occasion engaged in conduct directed at a specific person
That the defendant knew or should have known the person would regard as threatening bodily injury, death, or offense
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of family members
notes: Stalking is always a felony in Texas. Includes electronic communications and cyberstalking.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (against child under 18 with prior conviction)
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, alarm, abuse, torment, or embarrass another
Initiated communication and made an obscene comment, request, suggestion, or proposal
Or threatened bodily injury or damage to property
Or sent repeated electronic communications in a manner likely to harass
enhancements: Against a child under 18 (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Includes electronic communications. Repeated unwanted contact may escalate to stalking charges.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony (negligent); Second Degree Felony (reckless serious injury); First Degree Felony (intentional serious injury)
penalty_max: 10 years (Third Degree); 20 years (Second Degree); 99 years or life (First Degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence
Caused bodily injury to an elderly individual (65+)
Or failed to provide care causing bodily injury
enhancements: Intentional serious bodily injury (First Degree Felony)
notes: Elderly individual is defined as 65 or older. Exploitation of the elderly may be charged under § 32.53.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Third Degree Felony (in prohibited locations or while intoxicated)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly carried a handgun, illegal knife, or club
On or about their person
In a prohibited location or while otherwise ineligible
enhancements: On premises of school or polling place (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Texas allows permit-less carry for persons 21+ who are not prohibited. This statute applies to prohibited locations (bars, schools, government buildings) and prohibited persons.

statute_title: Unlawful Possession of Firearm by Felon
offense_class: Third Degree Felony; Second Degree Felony (before 5th anniversary of release or parole)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony
Possession occurred before the 5th anniversary of release from confinement or community supervision
enhancements: Possession within 5 years of release (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Felons may legally possess a firearm at their residence after the 5th anniversary of release. Federal law may still prohibit possession.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly carried a weapon
On the premises of a school, polling place, court, racetrack, secured airport area, or government meeting
notes: Carrying a weapon in prohibited locations is a Third Degree Felony regardless of carry permit status.

statute_title: Discharge of Firearm in Certain Municipalities
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Third Degree Felony (habitation)
elements: Defendant recklessly discharged a firearm
Inside the limits of a municipality having a population of 100,000 or more
enhancements: Discharge at or in the direction of a habitation, building, or vehicle (Third Degree Felony under § 22.05)
notes: Deadly conduct by discharging a firearm at or in the direction of persons, habitations, or vehicles is a Third Degree Felony under § 22.05.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use or Possession of Identifying Information
offense_class: State Jail Felony (under 5 items); Third Degree Felony (5-10 items); Second Degree Felony (10-50 items); First Degree Felony (50+ items)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third); 20 years (Second); 99 years or life (First)
elements: Defendant obtained, possessed, transferred, or used identifying information of another person
Without that person's consent
With intent to harm or defraud
notes: Classified by number of identifying items rather than dollar amount. Elderly victim enhancement raises offense one category.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant unlawfully appropriated the property
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement is prosecuted under the general theft statute in Texas. Misapplication of fiduciary property is also addressed in § 32.45.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); State Jail Felony (will, deed, mortgage, commercial instrument, credit card); Third Degree Felony (money, securities, stamps, government documents)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third Degree)
elements: Defendant forged a writing with intent to defraud or harm another
Including altering, making, completing, executing, or authenticating any writing so that it purports to be the act of another
notes: Forgery of a will, mortgage, deed, or commercial instrument is a State Jail Felony. Forgery of money or government documents is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony (money, securities, stamps)
elements: Defendant forged or counterfeited money, stamps, or securities
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting currency is also a federal crime. State charges under the forgery statute.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (under $20); Class B Misdemeanor ($20-$500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500); State Jail Felony ($1,500+)
penalty_max: Fine only to 2 years depending on amount
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check or similar instrument
Knowing at the time that the issuer did not have sufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Presumption of knowledge and intent if check not paid within 10 days of notice of dishonor.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (under $2,500); Third Degree Felony ($2,500-$30,000); Second Degree Felony ($30,000-$150,000); First Degree Felony ($150,000+)
elements: Defendant prepared or presented a statement in support of a claim for payment under an insurance policy
Knowing the statement contained materially false information
With intent to defraud
notes: Includes auto, health, life, and property insurance fraud. Value thresholds mirror theft statute.

statute_title: Credit Card or Debit Card Abuse
offense_class: State Jail Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to obtain a benefit fraudulently
Used a credit or debit card knowing it was not issued to them
Or was expired, canceled, revoked, or stolen
notes: Credit card abuse is always a State Jail Felony regardless of the amount. Includes using stolen card numbers.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (under $2,500); Third Degree Felony ($2,500-$30,000); Second Degree Felony ($30,000-$150,000); First Degree Felony ($150,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly acquired, maintained, or used proceeds of criminal activity
Or conducted or facilitated a transaction involving proceeds of criminal activity
notes: Texas money laundering statute mirrors federal law. Value thresholds determine classification.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained property by deception
Created a false impression of fact or value
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud prosecuted as theft. Texas also has specific fraud statutes for securities (§ 32.46), Medicaid (§ 35A), and telecommunications (§ 33.02).

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the penetration of another person
Without that person's consent
By force, threat, fraud, or while the victim was unconscious or unable to resist
enhancements: Use of a date rape drug
notes: Sexual assault in Texas is what many states call rape. Second Degree Felony with 2-20 year range.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed sexual assault as defined in § 22.011
And caused serious bodily injury or attempted to kill the victim
Or used or exhibited a deadly weapon
Or the victim was under 14, elderly, or disabled
notes: Aggravated sexual assault is Texas's most serious sexual offense. Minimum 25 years if victim is under 6. Lifetime sex offender registration.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant exposed their anus or genitals
With intent to arouse or gratify sexual desire
Knowing another person was present who would be offended or alarmed
notes: Indecent exposure is a Class B Misdemeanor regardless of number of offenses. Does not require sex offender registration for first offense.

offense_class: State Jail Felony (first); Third Degree Felony (second); Second Degree Felony (minor victim)
penalty_max: 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third Degree); 20 years (minor victim)
elements: Defendant knowingly offered or agreed to pay a fee to another person
For the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct
notes: Texas significantly increased prostitution solicitation penalties. First offense is now a State Jail Felony. Solicitation of a minor is a Second Degree Felony.

statute_title: Possession or Promotion of Child Pornography
offense_class: Third Degree Felony (possession); Second Degree Felony (promotion/distribution)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed or promoted material depicting a child under 18 in sexual conduct
Defendant knew the material depicted a child
notes: Possession is a Third Degree Felony. Promotion (distribution, sale) is a Second Degree Felony. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: State Jail Felony (first); Third Degree Felony (subsequent or reportable conviction involving child)
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant failed to comply with registration requirements
enhancements: Underlying offense involved a child (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Texas sex offender registration required for 10 years, lifetime, or civilly committed depending on offense.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused sexual penetration or contact with a child
The child was younger than 17
Regardless of consent
enhancements: Child under 14 (Aggravated Sexual Assault, First Degree Felony)
notes: Age of consent in Texas is 17. Sexual contact with a child under 17 is sexual assault regardless of consent. Under 14 triggers aggravated charges.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor; Class B Misdemeanor (firearm display)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly used abusive, indecent, profane, or vulgar language in a public place
Or made an offensive gesture likely to incite an immediate breach of the peace
Or created a hazardous or offensive condition by an act not serving a legitimate purpose
enhancements: Discharging a firearm in a public place (Class B Misdemeanor)
notes: Most disorderly conduct is a fine-only Class C Misdemeanor. Firearm discharge elevates to Class B.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Third Degree Felony (use of a deadly weapon)
elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or obstructed a person the defendant knew was a peace officer
From effecting an arrest, search, or transportation
By using force against the peace officer or another
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Requires force — passive resistance alone is not sufficient. Use of a deadly weapon elevates to Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor suspect); Third Degree Felony (felony suspect)
elements: Defendant, with intent to hinder the arrest, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another
Harbored or concealed the other person
Or provided a means of avoiding arrest or effecting escape
enhancements: Suspect charged with felony (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Obstruction charges vary in Texas depending on the underlying offense. Tampering with evidence (§ 37.09) is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Up to 6 months and $500 fine per act
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or engaged in disorderly conduct in the court's presence
Or interfered with orderly proceedings
notes: Texas courts have inherent contempt power. Both civil and criminal contempt available.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
To the degree that the defendant was a danger to themselves or others
notes: Fine-only offense. Officers may take the intoxicated person to a detoxification facility. No jail time for first offense.

statute_title: Bail Jumping and Failure to Appear
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying); Third Degree Felony (felony underlying)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal bond
Defendant failed to appear as required by the conditions of release
The failure was intentional
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Bail jumping is a separate offense. Bond forfeiture proceedings are separate from criminal charges.

statute_title: False Report to Peace Officer or Law Enforcement Employee
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (if report involves capital felony or felony of first degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false report to a peace officer
Or filed a false report with a law enforcement agency
enhancements: Report involves capital felony or first degree felony (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Filing a false police report is a Class B Misdemeanor. Enhanced if the false report involves a serious felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (threat of violence); Class A Misdemeanor (against family member/public servant); Third Degree Felony (threat to public, school, or critical infrastructure)
penalty_max: 180 days (Class B); 1 year (Class A); 10 years (Third Degree)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any offense involving violence to persons or property
With intent to place someone in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
Or cause impairment or interruption of public communications, transportation, or public utilities
notes: Terroristic threat covers a wide range from personal threats (misdemeanor) to public/school threats (Third Degree Felony).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant, with intent to deceive and with knowledge of the statement's meaning
Made a false statement under oath or affirmation
In any official proceeding
notes: Basic perjury is a Class A Misdemeanor. Aggravated perjury (§ 37.03) in an official proceeding relating to a criminal case or administrative proceeding is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly offered, conferred, or agreed to confer on another
Any benefit as consideration for the recipient's decision, opinion, recommendation, vote, or other exercise of discretion as a public servant
notes: Both the person offering and the public servant accepting may be charged. Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor custody); Third Degree Felony (felony custody); Second Degree Felony (use of force/weapon)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 10 years (Third Degree); 20 years (Second Degree)
elements: Defendant was in lawful custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody
enhancements: Use of force or a deadly weapon (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Escape sentence runs consecutively to any existing sentence. Includes escape from prison, jail, or custody of an officer.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (failure to provide care); State Jail Felony (torture/killing); Third Degree Felony (serious bodily injury or prior conviction)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 2 years (State Jail); 10 years (Third Degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly tortured, killed, or failed to provide necessary food, water, care, or shelter for an animal
In a cruel manner
notes: Texas has separate statutes for livestock and non-livestock animals. Animal fighting is covered under § 42.10.

offense_class: Determined by original offense classification
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on community supervision (probation)
Defendant violated one or more conditions of community supervision
notes: Court may revoke community supervision and impose any sentence originally available. Progressive sanctions may be used for technical violations.

statute_title: Violation of Parole or Mandatory Supervision
offense_class: Determined by original offense classification
elements: Defendant was released on parole or mandatory supervision
Defendant violated one or more conditions of release
notes: Board of Pardons and Paroles makes revocation decisions. Defendant may be returned to serve the remainder of the sentence.

statute_title: Criminal Responsibility for Conduct of Another (Parties to Offenses)
offense_class: Same as the principal offense
elements: A crime was committed by another person
Defendant, acting with intent to promote or assist the commission of the offense
Solicited, encouraged, directed, aided, or attempted to aid the other person
notes: Texas law of parties holds accomplices equally responsible. Conspiracy to commit a felony where a death occurs may result in capital murder charges for all parties.

offense_class: One category lower than the target offense; minimum State Jail Felony for felony attempts; minimum Class A Misdemeanor for Class A/B Misdemeanor attempts
penalty_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant, with specific intent to commit an offense
Did an act amounting to more than mere preparation
That tended but failed to effect the commission of the offense
notes: Criminal attempt is generally one category lower than the completed offense. Capital Felony attempt is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: One category lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of the target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons that they or one or more of them would engage in conduct constituting the offense
The defendant or one or more of them performed an overt act in pursuance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy is one category lower than the target offense. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is an affirmative defense.
